PREFIX acl: <http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#> PREFIX nfo: <http://www.semanticdesktop.org/ontologies/2007/03/22/nfo#> PREFIX sioc: <http://rdfs.org/sioc/ns#>
# what the authorization decision knows of a document, run on its dataspace's store: one (?Rel ?Target) row per thing an # authorization can name it by. Every row binds both columns, so a row can only join the branch of the ACL query its tag # selects - with an unbound column, a types-only row would join any acl:default grant. # acl:accessTo the document itself # acl:default each of its ancestors. A graph states the containment of its own document only, which the graph # store enforces, so a path over the union graph reads exactly what each document's graph says # acl:accessToClass each type the document's own graph asserts; no other graph can add to them. An uploaded file has # no graph of its own, and is typed nfo:FileDataObject and nothing else # acl:owner its owner, as its own graph states it, which decides lacl:OwnerAgent SELECT DISTINCT ?Rel ?Target WHERE { { BIND(acl:accessTo AS ?Rel) BIND($this AS ?Target) } UNION { GRAPH <urn:x-arq:UnionGraph> { $this (sioc:has_parent|sioc:has_container)+ ?Target } BIND(acl:default AS ?Rel) } UNION { GRAPH $this { $this a ?Target } BIND(acl:accessToClass AS ?Rel) } UNION { GRAPH ?g { $this a nfo:FileDataObject } FILTER NOT EXISTS { GRAPH $this { ?s ?p ?o } } BIND(acl:accessToClass AS ?Rel) BIND(nfo:FileDataObject AS ?Target) } UNION { GRAPH $this { $this acl:owner ?Target } BIND(acl:owner AS ?Rel) } }

PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> PREFIX acl: <http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#> PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
# the authorizations of the agent for a document, in either dataspace. An authorization counts only in the admin document # whose primary topic it is, and a group's members only in the group's own document: a statement anywhere else in the # admin dataset is not one an administrator made. The document is matched through the rows of the document context query # (see documentContextQuery): an authorization names it, a container above it (acl:default), or a class of it. # The pattern is evaluated once per row with ?Rel and ?Target bound, so the target match comes first: it looks up the few # authorizations naming the row, and every later part checks them instead of scanning the admin dataset again per row DESCRIBE ?auth WHERE { GRAPH ?g { { VALUES ?Rel { acl:accessTo acl:default } ?auth ?Rel ?Target } UNION { BIND(acl:accessToClass AS ?Rel) ?auth acl:accessToClass ?Class GRAPH <urn:x-arq:UnionGraph> { ?Target (rdfs:subClassOf)* ?Class } } ?g foaf:primaryTopic ?auth . ?auth acl:mode ?Mode . { ?auth acl:agent $agent } UNION { ?auth acl:agentGroup ?Group GRAPH ?groupG { ?groupG foaf:primaryTopic ?Group . ?Group foaf:member $agent } FILTER(strstarts(str(?groupG), str($base))) } UNION { ?auth acl:agentClass foaf:Agent } UNION { ?auth acl:agentClass $AuthenticatedAgentClass } UNION { ?auth acl:agentClass $OwnerAgentClass } } FILTER(strstarts(str(?g), str($base))) } # fail-closed default: with no document context injected, the only row is a tag no branch selects, so nothing matches. # DocumentContext.applyTo replaces this block with the document's rows VALUES (?Rel ?Target) { (rdfs:Resource rdfs:Resource) }

PREFIX sioc: <http://rdfs.org/sioc/ns#>
# a child of the document: one whose own graph points its containment at it. Containment asserted in any other graph # does not count - a document states its place in the hierarchy in its own graph, where PUT asserts it and no other # write can change it SELECT ?child WHERE { VALUES ?containment { sioc:has_parent sioc:has_container } GRAPH ?child { ?child ?containment $this } } LIMIT 1
DESCRIBE $this
